newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon to buy TI defense unit - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon to buy TI defense unit - WSJ.

text.p: Raytheon Co has agreed to acquire the defense electronics business of Texas Instruments Inc in a deal valued at nearly $3 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported Monday, citing sources familiar with the deal.
The story said Raytheon's move appears geared to position the company to launch a $9 billion bid in the coming days for the defense business of Hughes Electronics Corp, a unit of General Motors Corp.
Hughes is preparing to auction its defense electronics businees in the days ahead, the article noted. Final bids are due late Monday, the article said.
The Journal said Raytheon defeated a competing bid by Northrop Grumman Corp for the missile and defense electronics holdings of Texas Instruments.
The Raytheon acquisition of Texas Instruments' holdings was approved by the boards of both companies in meetings held Friday and Saturday, the story said.
A spokesman for Raytheon did not return calls to the Journal; Northrop Grumman declined to comment; and a representative for Texas Instruments couldn't be reached, the story said.

Raytheon is expected to pay cash for the unit as a means of minimizing the complications that would accompany two successive stock-for-stock deals, should the Hughes deal go through, the Journal said.
Raytheon is expected to fund the Texas Instruments acquisition by in part increasing debt that could push Raytheon's debt-to-equity ratio above 60 percent or more, the story said.
If Raytheon prevails in the Hughes deal, it would issue a large number of new shares for that transaction, the story said.

Texas Instruments had initially sought to be paid in Raytheon stock, but the Journal said Raytheon convinced the company that accepting a higher-than-expected cash payment would bring a large after-tax return while avoiding stock-for-stock uncertainties.
Allowing for tax benefits, Raytheon will have paid an amount closer to the $2.5 billion initially expected, the story said.

The story paints the latest acquisition against a backdrop of massive consolidation among U.S. military contractors in recent years, including deals such as last month's move by Boeing Co to buy McDonnell Douglas Corp.
